title: bug: staleLockReason compares the lock's resolved projectPath with the raw --project, so `--project //x` (Linux) or `/x` (native Windows) reads a live lock as 'projectPath mismatch'
description: After task-25ba449a, comparableProjectPath reads raw `//x` as UNC (Linux) and raw `/x` as POSIX (win32). The lock records path.resolve(projectPath) instead ('/x', 'C:\x'), so staleLockReason (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts) says 'projectPath mismatch' and removeStaleLock may delete a LIVE lock. This is reachable only in a start race before daemon.json exists; a daemon.json carrying those raw spellings is already foreign under isForeignDaemonInfo. Likely fix: compare against canonicalProjectPath(projectPath) in staleLockReason, with a regression row for each spelling.
definitionOfDone: staleLockReason never reports 'projectPath mismatch' for a lock written by the same --project spelling (raw //x on Linux, /x on native Windows, relative paths).
A regression test covers each spelling without touching the live .moe.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS ONLY. Load test-driven-development first.

Prerequisite: task-25ba449a is DONE (dependsOn).
- Confirm it landed: `git log moe/work-2026-10-24 --grep 'Moe-Task: task-25ba449ab87d4039a283426f07302cbc'`.
- Confirm staleLockReason in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts compares against `canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)`. If that line is absent, stop and call moe.request_replan naming it. This plan never edits index.ts.
- If 25ba449a's landed tests already assert staleLockReason's reason for every spelling below plus the mismatch control, add only the rows that are missing.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts:
- Add `staleLockReason` to the `./index.js` import list.
- Add X15 right after X14, inside `describe('native aliases of --project')`, and reuse that block's fixture:
  - beforeEach chdirs to path.dirname(testDir) and builds `alias`: POSIX `/${testDir}` (raw //x), or on win32 testDir without its drive, with / separators (/x on the cwd's drive);
  - afterEach restores the cwd;
  - the enclosing block supplies DEAD_PID and lockPath().
  If 25ba449a reshaped that block, put X15 wherever the alias/cwd fixture lives.
- Spellings: canonical testDir, alias, relative path.basename(testDir), and dotted `./${base}/`.
- For each WRITER spelling:
  (1) acquireLock(writer) is true.
  (2) Every READER spelling gets staleLockReason(reader) === null. The owner is this live process and the lock is fresh.
  (3) Rewrite only the lock JSON's pid to DEAD_PID, keeping acquireLock's projectPath and createdAt. Every reader then gets exactly 'lock owner not alive'. The mismatch check runs before the liveness check, so this proves the path comparison passed.
  (4) fs.rmSync(lockPath()) before the next writer.
- Compare [writer, reader, reason] tuples, so a failure names the spelling pair.
- Control: write a fresh lock with a live pid, recorded for path.join(testDir, 'moved'). Every reader gets 'projectPath mismatch'. This pins that branch, so 'never mismatch' can't be met by deleting the check.
- Error handling in the test: failures must surface, never be swallowed.
  - No try/catch around assertions or fs calls.
  - Clean up with fs.rmSync WITHOUT force, so a lock at the wrong path throws.
  - Never use releaseLock for this: it ignores unlink errors and would hide a wrong path.
  - JSON.parse of the lock lets a malformed lock throw.
- Rules:
  - mkdtemp testDir only, never the live .moe;
  - no process.platform or path spies (the alias is native on each OS);
  - no child process (X14 owns contention);
  - no new helper or file;
  - X1-X14 stay unchanged.

Mutation proof, only in your scratch snapshot copy (never the shared tree, never committed):
(a) staleLockReason compares the raw projectPath: every tuple with an alias reader must fail by assertion.
(b) Delete the mismatch line: the control must fail.
Keep both outputs.

comments.author: worker-5ebbf433
comments.content:
Correction from the filer (worker-5ebbf433), 2026-10-30: this description understates the reach. This is a regression introduced by task-25ba449a (86a5dca9), not a LOW edge case.

1. Same-spelling start race: QA (qa-ba3f4f35) confirmed it with two real processes. The repro is /tmp/qa25ba-lock-race.mjs, with logs in /tmp/qa25ba-race-{candidate,parent}.log. On the candidate, B replaces live A's lock for raw //tmp/x. On the parent, reason=null and acquireLock=false.

2. Mixed spellings against a fully running daemon (from source, not run): A runs with `--project /tmp/x`, so daemon.json and the lock both record '/tmp/x'. B then starts with `--project //tmp/x` on Linux. The native-Windows equivalent is A on `C:\x` and B on `/x` from a C: cwd. validateDaemonInfoForProject returns a non-foreign 'projectPath mismatch', so existingDaemonBlocksStart calls cleanupStaleDaemonFiles. That deletes A's live daemon.json, and staleLockReason's mismatch unlinks A's lock. B then starts a second state writer on the next port. On the parent, both spellings compare equal.

Fix direction: compare against canonicalProjectPath(projectPath) (native path.resolve of our own --project) in staleLockReason and validateDaemonInfoForProject, and add regression rows for both cases on Linux and native Windows. This belongs in the 25ba449a reopen. Once that lands, this row is a duplicate.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Regression coverage only; no runtime change. staleLockReason judges a lock written by acquireLock under any spelling of the project's own directory by its owner, never as 'projectPath mismatch'. The spellings are canonical absolute, the native alias (raw //x on Linux, drive-less /x on native Windows), relative x and ./x/. The owner verdicts are: null when the owner is live and the lock fresh, 'lock owner not alive' when the owner is dead. A lock recorded for another directory still reads 'projectPath mismatch'.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Archive as a duplicate of 25ba449a. Rejected: the human re-promoted the row at 14:24Z, and its DoD names relative spellings plus a direct staleLockReason guarantee that 25ba449a's X12-X14 never assert.
2. Fold the rows into 25ba449a. Rejected: that task is in its final self-review under a size budget, and both would edit the same file at once.

4. A real-process contention matrix. Rejected: X14 already has one. An in-process owner (this live pid) tests the reason function deterministically and cheaply.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- staleLockReason (index.ts ~220) checks in this order: malformed, foreign (null), projectPath mismatch, owner not alive, timeout. So a dead-owner lock's reason shows whether the path check passed.
- acquireLock records canonicalProjectPath(projectPath), which is path.resolve.
- comparableProjectPath resolves only relative input. An absolute //x is read as UNC on every OS, and /x as POSIX. That is why raw aliases mismatched while relative spellings always matched, so the relative rows are a regression guard, not a red test.
- 25ba449a's describe('native aliases of --project') is nested in 'daemon.json across the WSL boundary', so DEAD_PID, lockPath() and jsonPath() are in scope.
- staleLockReason is already in index.ts's named exports.
- tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, and vitest transpiles with esbuild, so neither the build nor vitest typechecks the test file. Keep types simple.
planningNotes.risks:
- 25ba449a's QA loop may reshape the native-aliases block. This row is claimable only after 25ba449a is DONE, so adapt the placement rather than waiting or editing its rows.
- isEpicFinal:true here is only highest-order drift: the epic is a perpetual bucket with no finalTaskId (mem:decision-epic-final-designation). The regression scope is the full daemon package suite, not a whole-epic pass.
- The Windows leg needs a Windows snapshot.
- Residual aliases that path.resolve can't fold (symlinks/junctions, 8.3 names, \\?\, case-insensitive macOS volumes) are pre-existing and out of scope.
